candidates.summary: BBC North West Tonight's Roger Johnson says the response is "what Children in Need is all about"

candidates.lead: BBC North West Tonight's Roger Johnson says the response is "what Children in Need is all about"
candidates.evidence_text: Roger's colleagues step up after injury ends BBC presenter's running challenge - BBC News Image caption, Roger Johnson called on his colleagues to unite for Children in Need By Roger Johnson North West Tonight Published 1 hour ago I'm not much of a runner. I never have been. But I have been getting my trainers on most mornings for the past 18 months, simply to stay fit and lose weight. So, I wasn't too daunted when I was challenged to run 41km (26.2 miles) over the space of two weeks for this year's BBC Children in Need appeal. Lots of people do a marathon in one go so how hard could it be? Well, perhaps I shouldn't have been so conceited. Four weeks ago, a long-standing foot problem flared up. I iced it. I raised it. The doctor gave me pills. I even had an x-ray. But it stubbornly refused to get better. Members of Lostock Athletics Club had kindly offered to run the first few miles with me, and it was arranged for a drizzly Tuesday morning in Blackrod, near Horwich. I arrived, hobbling, and had to watch bemused as they jogged off into the distance without me. Ian Burns, who is in his late 60s, offered some words of wisdom. "We are a bit stubborn and think we're not really hurt when we really are," he said. "It can take me weeks to get over a small injury, whereas 10 years ago, I would have been a couple of days." Image caption, It was a team effort to complete the Children in Need challenge Either way, I hoped I would soon be fit to start the challenge. I waited and waited. It felt as though I was taking painkillers like sweets (while never exceeding the recommended dose, of course). But by the end of October, still unable to manage more than a hobble, I needed a Plan B. And that was when, as I looked around the BBC North West Tonight newsroom, I realised salvation could be close at hand. Could a few colleagues join forces to run the miles on my behalf? I sent an email asking for help. Image caption, More than 30 people ran more 160 miles between them The essence of Children in Need, since it started in 1980, has been about strangers coming together to raise money to help others. Over the decades, I've met so many fundraisers and those they help. I've heard stories which have made me laugh and cry. I will always remember an elderly lady in Bootle, Merseyside, who had just collected her pension and insisted on putting £20 in a collection bucket as we walked down the north west coast. And Ella, supported by a bereavement charity on the Isle of Man, after her brother died. There are countless others. Image caption, Colleagues put their best foot forward to complete the challenge Generosity runs through it all - money, of course, but also generosity of time and spirit. So maybe I shouldn't have been surprised when my colleagues started replying to my email. In the end, more than 30 ran more 160 miles between them. Far more than my target. The power of the collective uniting for a common cause. It's what Children in Need is all about. But it's also taught me another lesson - if I'm asked again to do something for the cause next year, I will promise to be a little less complacent. Children in Need 2026 will be broadcast live on BBC iPlayer and BBC One at 19:00 GMT on Friday 13 November. candidates.evidence_text: Landlady says up to 60 teenagers attacked pub with fireworks - BBC News Image caption, Paula said she had to lock 30 customers inside her pub By Georgie Docker North West Published 4 November 2026 A landlady said she locked customers inside her pub for hours while a group of teenagers attacked it with fireworks. Salford pub manager Paula, 61, said she and 30 customers hid out as "about 60 teenagers" bombarded The Plough, in Cadishead, on Saturday. Police were called, and footage from the incident, appearing to show doors being kicked and a bus driver being assaulted, has since been shared on social media. "It was very scary. I'm worried they will come back," Paula said. Paula, who has been in charge at The Plough for 10 months, said she had "never seen anything like it", and that she feared the attack was "organised". "It started with just a few of them," she said. "But more starting coming and then there was 60 of them." Paula said the teenagers began by targeting "anyone passing" on the main road, including families out trick-or-treating. Greater Manchester Police Ch Insp Lee Gridley said the force would not "tolerate anti-social behaviour in our communities". "We will relentlessly tackle criminality, disrupt ASB and improve safety for local communities," he said. A force spokesperson said inquiries were ongoing to identify those responsible. Image caption, Paula said the incident followed a similar one where the gang had targeted doors on the high street The landlady said the pub became a target after she refused some teens use of the toilets, having told them children were not allowed in after 19:00. "They were all bombarding my door, trying to burn all my [Halloween] decorations, firing fireworks at the pub windows, throwing bangers under cars, and no-one could do anything about it," she said. "There was too many of them." She said she also saw the group throwing a brick at a bus. Image caption, Paula said she thought the gang had organised the Cadishead meet-up over social media She said she was worried about a potential repeat of the trouble on Bonfire Night on Thursday. There was also trouble outside the nearby Coach and Horses pub, which plans to lock its doors on Thursday over concerns for staff and customers' safety. The manager of the pub told the BBC that a week before, there had been "11 police cars and two vans" out dealing with teenagers causing trouble. "Police need to be out on patrol because it has just got out of hand," they added. Image caption, The manager at The Coach and Horses said the behaviour "irritates all of us" Sue, who lives locally, said about 40 teens had been roaming around near her home on Thursday. She said she now keeps a canister of hairspray and her late husband's walking stick to hand to protect herself. The 73-year-old, who lives alone, said they "kick my door in at least two or three times a week - not just kicking it - properly booting it". "They all wear balaclavas and bandanas," she said. She said she was now wary of going out at night. "I'm thinking of just selling up and going. "I've loved this house and the area. "It is a big community area and all the people get on really well. "It's just these kids." Image caption, Sue said she kept hairspray and a walking stick to hand to defend herself Other residents said they had experienced similar trouble, with fireworks being shot at buildings and doors being kicked. Leonie, 21, who works on the high street, said she was frightened to go to work on Sunday after seeing videos of the gang attacking a bus driver on Saturday night. "I was worried about going into work," she said. "The shutters are on the inside of the windows. "It is so scary. "They all wear black as well so you can't see them." Image caption, David said he saw the group setting off fireworks from his upstairs window on Saturday David Hughes, 77, who has lived in the area for more than 40 years, said it had been "going on for months and months". "Groups of them wearing balaclavas and riding round on electric bikes," he said. "It's intimidating. "I used to go out to walk the dog in the evening but now when it gets to 17:00, I don't go out because it's not worth it. "And I don't think I'm the only one." I'm worried they will come back," Paula said Paula, who has been in charge at The Plough for 10 months, said she had "never seen anything like it", and that she feared the attack was "organised" "It started with just a few of them," she said. "But more starting coming and then there was 60 of them."

candidates.lead: Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 on a weed removal programme
candidates.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

candidates.evidence_text: Two more arrests have been made in an investigation into £1m of alleged financial irregularities at the University of Greater Manchester, formerly named the University of Bolton, between 2014 and 2025 Two men, in their 50s and 60s, have been arrested on suspicion of witness intimidation, perverting the course of justice and fraud by the abuse of position after raids in Bolton and South Yorkshire, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said One of the men was previously arrested on suspicion of money laundering in July, along with another man and a woman GMP said it was "exploring evidence indicating over £1m worth of fraudulent activity", including 60 transactions and more than a million emails The force started the investigation last year into "serious allegations of fraud and bribery" at the university after a report by the Manchester Mill , external and a subsequent report from Price Waterhouse Cooper commissioned by the university's Fraud Response Panel Two men in their 60s and a woman in her 50s who were arrested in July were released on bail under investigation

candidates.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

The election was prompted by the resignation of the former councillor on October 23 The day before, the Manchester Evening News reported Mr Quigg who has been a councillor for Royton North since 2022, had resigned from Reform UK mid-investigation . This was confirmed by the party in an official statement Mr Quigg was one of Reform’s first councillors in the borough alongside Sandra Ball and Mark Wilkinson. He led the group into the 2026 local elections where the party won 13 out of the 20 seats available and the most votes He was replaced as leader of the borough's second largest group in September by Mark Wilkinson who himself resigned later that month citing health issues. candidates.evidence_text: Money Manchester firm that took £123,000 from struggling businesses shut down The firm wrongly told companies that they could avoid reputational damage by selling their companies before liquidation - while charging fees of up to £6,800 Add to preferre A Manchester firm that took £123,000 from 51 struggling businesses was shut down by the High Court on Thursday (October 29). Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Company fined £600k after man killed by falling truck he was changing tyres on beside M56 21-year-old Niall Fawcett had been in his role less than four months when tragedy struck Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Report A tyre firm has been hit with a six-figure fine after one of its employees was killed by a falling truck while changing the tyre on a truck at the side of the M56 Niall Fawcett, 21, had been in his role at Lodge Tyre Company Limited - now known as Halford Commercial Fleet Services, a subsidiary of Halfords - for less than four months when he was called out to replace a blown-out tyre on the slip road at junction 7 of the M56 near Bowdon on While positioned below the truck, which was said to be low profile, it slipped from the jack holding it up and landed on Mr Fawcett, tragically causing fatal injuries The Health and Safety Executive said that Mr Fawcett's employer 'had not properly assessed the risks' associated with replacing tyres on a low-profile vehicle Halford Commercial Fleet Services Limited, of Icknield Street Drive, Washford West, Redditch, Worcestershire B98 0DE, pleaded guilty to breaching Section 2(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 at Warrington Magistrates' Court yesterday (November 3)

candidates.evidence_text: Crime Company fined £600k after man killed by falling truck he was changing tyres on beside M56 21-year-old Niall Fawcett had been in his role less than four months when tragedy struck Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Report A tyre firm has been hit with a six-figure fine after one of its employees was killed by a falling truck while changing the tyre on a truck at the side of the M56 Niall Fawcett, 21, had been in his role at Lodge Tyre Company Limited - now known as Halford Commercial Fleet Services, a subsidiary of Halfords - for less than four months when he was called out to replace a blown-out tyre on the slip road at junction 7 of the M56 near Bowdon on While positioned below the truck, which was said to be low profile, it slipped from the jack holding it up and landed on Mr Fawcett, tragically causing fatal injuries The Health and Safety Executive said that Mr Fawcett's employer 'had not properly assessed the risks' associated with replacing tyres on a low-profile vehicle Halford Commercial Fleet Services Limited, of Icknield Street Drive, Washford West, Redditch, Worcestershire B98 0DE, pleaded guilty to breaching Section 2(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 at Warrington Magistrates' Court yesterday (November 3)

candidates.evidence_text: NHS More strikes expected at four Greater Manchester hospitals after staff reject pay offer Nearly all theatre staff voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's offer Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Write More strikes are expected at a crisis-hit NHS trust after hundreds of theatre staff overwhelmingly rejected its latest offer in a long-running dispute over overtime pay Nearly all (99 per cent) of more than 400 theatre staff, including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, working across four hospitals voted to reject the Northern Care Alliance's (NCA) offer The Trust, which runs Salford Royal, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield General Hospital in Bury , said it was "very disappointing" that workers had rejected what it described as its "best offer" to end the dispute Trade union Unison, which represents the striking workers, said staff had sent a "resounding message" to NCA bosses and confirmed staff would continue to strike The dispute centres on the use of an outside agency called NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage additional shifts, with Unison claiming the arrangements could leave some workers earning up to £80 less per shift than under previous arrangements

candidates.evidence_text: Money Manchester firm that took £123,000 from struggling businesses shut down The firm wrongly told companies that they could avoid reputational damage by selling their companies before liquidation - while charging fees of up to £6,800 Add to preferre A Manchester firm that took £123,000 from 51 struggling businesses was shut down by the High Court on Thursday (October 29). Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of companies with debts by providing 'misleading services', the government's Insolvency Service has said The Manchester-registered company was found to be offering 'alternatives' to formal insolvency to directors of the companies in financial difficulty. It offered to arrange sales of 'financially distressed' businesses for £1 whilst charging fees of between £2,500 and £6,800 It comes following an Insolvency Service investigation which has subsequently led to the firm being shut down Insolvency Service Chief Investigator, David Usher, said: "Clark Sinclair Limited took advantage of struggling businesses by offering directors a misleading route out of their company’s debts, charging thousands of pounds for the service "Selling a company does not prevent its former directors’ conduct from being investigated if it later enters liquidation

His behaviour continued after he was taken into custody, where he spat in the faces of two police officers and elbowed one officer in the face Longworth, of Kemble Close, Horwich, appeared at Preston Magistrates' Court on October 22, where he admitted racially aggravated harassment and two counts of assaulting a police officer

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A predatory offender who targeted men has been sentenced after a survivor bravely came forward and helped secure his conviction Saleh Mahmud aged 30 of Canterbury Street, Ashton Under Lyne, was yesterday sentenced to 12 years’ imprisonment at Manchester Crown Court after being found guilty of two counts of rape and pleading guilty to robbery, common assault, two counts of fraud, intentional strangulation On 23 December 2025, the survivor met Mahmud during a night out in Manchester city centre. The following day, after travelling to Oldham together, Mahmud led him to a secluded wooded area in Failsworth where, despite the survivor making it clear he did not want to have sex, Mahmu After the attack, Mahmud threatened to kill the survivor and stole his mobile phone and bank cards before leaving. Once he felt safe to do so, the survivor reported the offence to police and provided forensic samples, which resulted in a DNA match identifying Mahmud Mahmud was arrested at his home address on 29 December 2025. A search of the property uncovered five mobile phones, snap bags containing white powder, more than £3,300 in cash and three driving licences belonging to other people. These items linked Mahmud to a separate robbery re In that incident, another man reported meeting Mahmud on a night out before returning to his home. Mahmud stole his mobile phone and wallet, assaulted him and fled the address

candidates.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.lead: Altrincham BID has teamed up with the Little Green Sock Project
candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham businesses join forces to bring Christmas cheer to children in need Skip to content News — Charity Altrincham businesses join forces to bring Christmas cheer to children in need Altrincham BID has teamed up with the Little Green Sock Project. , and David Prior November 4, 2026 . 11:44 AM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Businesses across Altrincham are joining forces to help ensure local children and families in need have something special to look forward to this Christmas. Altrincham BID, the organisation behind Visit Altrincham, has teamed up with the Little Green Sock Project to bring its Magical Christmas Gift Appeal to the town. The initiative will see Christmas trees appear in shops and businesses across Altrincham, each decorated with special gift tags representing a local child who might otherwise go without a present this Christmas. Customers, staff and visitors are invited to take a tag from one of the trees, buy the gift listed and return it unwrapped to the participating business. The Little Green Sock Project will then collect the presents, match them with children referred to the charity by trusted local professionals and ensure they are delivered in time for Christmas. All donated gifts must be returned before November 30. Jake Shoes was the first Altrincham business to put up its Magical Christmas Tree, with more now appearing across the town. Among the businesses taking part are Altytude Fitness, Aura Music Academy, Bridgfords Estate Agents, Circle Funerals, Goose Green Dental, Jake Shoes, Lund Bennett Law, Mabel's Cafe & Tea Room, Mathnasium of Altrincham, Myerson Solicitors, Oyez Arts at Altrincham Town Hall, Physical Fitness, Santander, Tesco Extra and The Stretch Station. Customers, staff and visitors are invited to take a tag from one of the trees, buy the gift listed and return it unwrapped to the participating business Altspace Coworking Office, Jobtrain, OMNI RMS and Realm Recruitment are also supporting the campaign by hosting trees for staff and clients. Kate Gerbich, from Altrincham BID, said: "We're delighted to be working with the Little Green Sock Project on this lovely initiative. "Christmas is a special time of year, but we know it can also be a difficult for some families. "By bringing our local businesses and community together, we hope to make a real difference and ensure more local children have something special to open on Christmas morning." Sophie Bell, from the Little Green Sock Project, said the support of Altrincham businesses and residents would make a real difference to families facing a difficult festive period. "Every gift tag represents a child who might otherwise go without something special this Christmas," she said. "The kindness and generosity of local businesses, their customers and the wider community will help bring smiles to children's faces and make a real difference to families who need a little extra support. "It's wonderful to see the community coming together to spread some Christmas magic." candidates.evidence_text: Manchester will come together under one sky this weekend as free fireworks celebrations return to light up the night sky on Saturday 7 November at three Manchester parks: Heaton Park, Wythenshawe Park and Platt Fields Park This year's events have been designed with sustainability, affordability and accessibility at their heart, ensuring the celebrations can be enjoyed by as many people as possible Affordability is a key focus, with a range of free activities and entertainment on offer throughout the evening and people are encouraged to take part in the Lantern Parade at 7pm prior to the main firework display. Visitors can also enjoy value-for-money funfair rides, with 95% The events have been planned to cater for a wide audience, including those who would prefer to attend an earlier, shorter, lower-noise display. Hosting three large-scale events across the city also helps reduce the environmental impact associated with multiple smaller community d A number of measures have been introduced to improve sustainability. Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. Local s In a bid to reduce food waste, any surplus food will, where possible, be redistributed through local charities and community projects in partnership with the Our Manchester Food Partnership

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Council can announce that Portland Street will be reopened to traffic from the early hours of Wednesday morning (November 4) This follows an extensive programme of emergency repairs due to a broken water main which ruptured last week A large-scale operation was put into action to isolate the source of the leak and repair it, and then carry out a full repair and resurface of the damaged road Crews from United Utilities and the Council have worked around the clock since Friday afternoon to ensure that the road could be reopened as quickly and safely as possible. This has been alongside TfGM staff who have also put additional resource into redirecting affected public t Illustrating the scale of the repairs needed, roughly 600 tonnes of road surface has been planed away and replaced over the course of these works The restrictions on the road are planned to be removed early on Wednesday morning (November 4), with the road practicably useable to motorists shortly after that

candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council will hold a meeting on November 10 to consider national changes to the planning system Last year, the government updated the National Scheme of Delegation for planning applications Under the changes, which come into effect on October 31, more applications would be decided by planning officers rather than by a committee of elected members The government has said this would make planning applications quicker, more efficient and reduce the number of decisions overturned on appeal Larger and more contentious applications would still need approval from planning committees For these changes to be implemented in Bolton, there must first be an amendment to the council constitution agreed by a vote at Full Council

candidates.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

Founded in 1597, Wigan Grammar School taught countless pupils in a history spanning almost four centuries and served as one of the town’s oldest continuously operating institu On Wednesday 28th October, a selection of former pupils, Wigan Council and Wrightington, Wigan, and Leigh NHS Trust representatives attended the unveiling of the blue plaque at the Thomas Linacre Centre, which housed the school from 1937 until its closure in 1972. Councillor Chri “This blue plaque is a fitting recognition of the school’s remarkable legacy, ensuring that its story is remembered and celebrated for years to come.” Gaining a reputation for excellence that persisted through the centuries, Wigan Grammar School’s pupils have been represented in fields as diverse as neurology, print making, engineering and nuclear energy Some famous alumni include acclaimed composer Sir Ernest Bullock as well as actor Sir Ian McKellen

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . The city comes alive with a plethora of family-friendly activities, ensuring that children of all ages have a memorable and joyful experience. For a touch of outdoor fun, enjoy the green spaces in Heaton Park, complete with play areas, a farm, and scenic picnicking spots. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. candidates.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:40 Early Bird: £30 General Admission: £35 Late Bird: £40 18+ P.S. candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

From 10am to 4pm, The Makers Market takes over Market Place, right in the heart of SK1, with 65+ independent traders selling handmade goods, artisan food and one-off finds against the backdrop of Stockport's Think craft, ceramics, prints, jewellery, candles, street food, and the kind of things you won't find anywhere else. It's a good chance to get some early Christmas shopping done too. Entry's free, it's dog-friendly and there's seating on-site, so you can take your time having a m Getting there: Stockport Interchange is the nearest bus stop, about a 12-minute walk away. There are cycle racks on-site. Parking nearby is limited, so check Parkopedia for the closest spaces 🗓 Saturday 10 October, 10am to 4pm (second Saturday of every month)

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Researchers argue that universities need to move beyond treating AI primarily as a technical challenge or a threat to academic integrity, and develop a better understanding of how students and staff engage with it. The research examined how academic staff and students perceived their own use of generative AI tools, as well as their views of how the technology was being used in higher education. The study surveyed 45 academic staff and 86 students in a school covering social science disciplines at a UK research-intensive university. The questionnaires were conducted between April and June 2024, so essentially before AI took over the likes of Google whether you asked it to or not. When asked about students’ use of AI for academic purposes, staff gave an average rating of 5.23 on a seven-point scale. Students’ own responses produced an average of just 3.11. The researchers caution that students may have underreported their use of AI, but say the difference nevertheless points to the limited information staff may have about how students use these tools in their studies. AI use can be difficult for lecturers to identify, particularly when they see only the final version of an assignment rather than the process through which it was produced. Students may also use AI independently of their interactions with teaching staff, leaving academics with an incomplete picture of their working practices. The research also found that students were generally more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI. Students rated the technology more highly in terms of its likely contribution to academic performance, including helping them learn about their subjects, increasing productivity and reducing workloads. They also felt more strongly than staff that appropriate conditions and support were in place to help them use AI tools. Among the uses identified in the survey, students reported using generative AI to find answers to questions and assignments, generate written work, and translate or improve the grammar of their writing. The researchers suggest that the immediate appeal of AI tools may lie in their ability to produce and improve text. However, they also argue that universities need to understand the range of ways students use the technology, rather than assume that its role in academic work is straightforward. The study also found considerable variation in staff members’ familiarity with AI. While 63 per cent of academic staff respondents had used at least one generative AI tool in the six months before the survey, some had limited practical experience of the technology. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Posted on November 4, 2026 by staff Manchester FinTech Crediflow AI secures £1.5m Startup which came through PXN’s PraeSeed programme last year aims to cut manual work behind commercial lending through automation Share: Listen to article FinTech Investment A FinTech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million in funding. Manchester-based Crediflow AI automates the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. The company has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts – a process the industry calls financial spreading – analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. The funding will accelerate development of the company’s platform, support engineering and product hires, and help Crediflow serve more banks and specialist lenders. Crediflow will also extend automation across the loan lifecycle, with workflows tailored to each lender’s credit policies and processes. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs. “Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work,” said Kenfack. “When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. We built Crediflow to bring that workload down and give credit teams more time to understand the borrower and structure the financing.” Last year, Crediflow became one of eight companies to receive funding from PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based investment programme run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II to help scale early-stage businesses. Revolut valuation reaches whopping £85bn after latest fundraising Joe Ball, senior investment associate at PXN Ventures, said: “Businesses of all sizes and across all sectors often rely on commercial finance for a multitude of reasons, but the processes involved in granting this finance are often largely manual, making the process inefficient and slowing down lending decisions. “By automating this area of the sector, Drey and the Crediflow AI team are not just supporting lenders but also removing barriers for companies that need funding to grow.” Jonathan Keeling, partner at Haatch, said: “The best B2B founders build the product they wished they’d had in their last job. candidates.lead: FinTech giant Revolut has announced the close of its latest fundraising process, establishing a new company valuation of $115 billion (£85bn).
candidates.evidence_text: Revolut valuation reaches whopping £85bn after latest fundraising Posted on November 4, 2026 by staff Revolut valuation reaches whopping £85bn after latest fundraising London-headquartered company with 80m retail customers around world targets 100m in more than 100 countries Share: Listen to article FinTech giant Revolut has announced the close of its latest fundraising process, establishing a new company valuation of $115 billion (£85bn). Just a year ago, an employee share sale valued Revolut at $75bn . The transaction was led by Glade Brook Capital Partners, Coatue, Durable Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., and Baillie Gifford – with participation from both long-standing partners and new global investors. The London-headquartered firm, which has 80 million retail customers around the world, recently announced that it had secured its 34th banking licence in New Zealand . This year the company has also launched banks in the UK, Mexico and Australia, while securing banking licences in France, Colombia, and Argentina, alongside conditional US charter approval. This builds on Revolut’s established European banking operations across 30 markets. Revolut’s 2025 revenue grew 46% to $6bn (£4.5bn) and pre-tax profit climbed 57% to $2.3bn (£1.7bn), expanding pre-tax margins to 38%. The company’s long-term goal is to serve over 100m active customers across more than 100 countries. “Every bank we launch means more people get a better way to manage their money, wherever they live,” said Nik Storonsky, CEO and founder. “Our team makes that happen, and employee ownership has been central to our culture from day one. “That’s why we’ve once again given them the chance to share in the value they’ve created, as we work towards our next milestone of serving 100 million customers.” Victor Stinga, CFO of Revolut, said: “The milestones achieved this year have been several years in the making. They allow us to strengthen our digital banking proposition in our core markets and pave the way for it reaching millions more customers beyond Europe. “The confidence of our investors, both existing and new, reflects Revolut’s unique opportunity to build the first truly global bank.” Andy Burnham’s first 100 days: Hope, hype or real change? candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Art Fair has announced details of a prestigious three-night chef residency ahead of its much-anticipated return to the city later this month Combining the worlds of contemporary art and fine dining, the fair, which runs from Thu 19 Nov – Sun 22 Nov , will host Cumbria’s Michelin-starred The Forest Side and Head Chef Paul Leonard In what will be the restaurant’s first Manchester residency, Leonard will create bespoke dining experiences for leading art buyers, collectors and VIP guests at Manchester Central. The partnership is a significant expansion of last year’s collaboration, which saw Leonard and Manc At The Forest Side in Grasmere, Leonard is renowned for his creative, ingredient-led approach to modern British cuisine, drawing inspiration from the Cumbrian landscape and its seasonal produce, including ingredients grown and foraged from the restaurant’s 45-acre grounds Under his leadership, the restaurant has retained its Michelin Star, first awarded in 2016, and was awarded a Michelin Green Star earlier this year in recognition of its commitment to sustainability and ingredient provenance. The hotel also received a Michelin Key in 2024 The initiative has been championed by Manchester Art Fair Executive Chair Thom Hetherington, who was previously involved in the launch of Restaurant magazine and The World’s 50 Best Restaurants Awards

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. The 54-year-old has been touted as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick if he is sacked, but Emery instead looks set to sign a new long-term contract at Villa Carrick eased pressure on his shoulders on Tuesday evening as United came from behind to beat AS Roma in the Champions League at Old Trafford . Emery and Villa head to United's home next, with that Premier League clash set to take place on Sunday afternoon Villa will be looking to respond to a disappointing last two results with defeat away to Barcelona coming after a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham. Though Emery's side have flattered to deceive in the last week, it remains clear that he has drastically improved their fortunes since joi As a result of that, unsurprisingly, Villa want to keep him for the foreseeable and that hope has been reflected by a meeting on Wednesday between key members of the club over his future In a notably candid club statement, Villa confirmed that there were "positive discussions" between Emery, chairman Nassef Sawiris, President of Football Operations Roberto Olabe and Director of Football Operations Damian Vidagany

candidates.lead: BOOMBOX | London | Electric Brixton | 03.12.2026 | 20:00 at Electric Brixton
candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
